config.title: Board State

intro.title: Board State
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build the foundation for a Tic-Tac-Toe game by implementing board state management in Angular. You'll learn how to represent game data using TypeScript arrays and objects, and how to track the current state of the game board. The core programming concept focuses on state management - storing, updating, and displaying dynamic data that changes as users interact with your application. You'll work with Angular components, TypeScript data structures, and property binding to create a reactive game board that updates in real-time. By the end of this lesson, you'll have a functional game board that can display X's and O's in the correct positions and track whose turn it is to play.
intro.usecase: Board state management is essential in interactive applications like project management tools (Trello, Asana), chess or game platforms, and data visualization dashboards where users manipulate grid-based content. In Angular applications, you'll implement board state when building kanban boards, calendar interfaces, seating charts, or any UI where items can be moved, added, or removed from specific positions. This pattern is also crucial for form builders, spreadsheet-like interfaces, and inventory management systems where tracking the position and status of elements across a structured layout is required. Enterprise dashboards frequently use board state to manage widget placement, allowing users to customize their workspace by dragging and rearranging components.

objectives: Initialize a two-dimensional array structure to represent the game board state
Implement methods to update individual cell values within the board matrix
Configure TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of board state data
Apply array manipulation techniques to modify board contents programmatically
Bind board state data to Angular template elements for visual display
Construct helper functions to validate and control board state transitions
Integrate board state management with Angular component lifecycle methods
Render dynamic board layouts based on current state values

steps.title: Import Angular Component and OnInit
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Component and OnInit from Angular core. Both are needed for creating components with lifecycle hooks.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple items from a library
import { Router, ActivatedRoute } from '@angular/router';
steps.expectedOutcome: Angular Component and OnInit are imported and ready to use for creating a component that can manage board state
successCriteria: Component and OnInit are imported from '@angular/core'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing both Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'. Both will be needed for this lesson.
steps.feedbackWrong: Not quite right. You need to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core' using the import statement. Check the syntax for importing multiple items from a module.

steps.title: Create BoardComponent class
steps.instruction: Create a BoardComponent class that implements OnInit and export it
steps.hint: In Angular, create a class using the 'class' keyword, implement the OnInit interface, and export the class so it can be used elsewhere
steps.seedCode:
// Import Angular dependencies here

// Create your BoardComponent class here
steps.expectedOutcome: A BoardComponent class is created that implements the OnInit interface and is exported
successCriteria: BoardComponent class is created, implements OnInit interface, and is exported
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your class implements the OnInit interface and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a class named BoardComponent that implements OnInit and export it for use in other parts of the application.

steps.title: Initialize board state property
steps.instruction: Add a board property to your BoardComponent class and initialize it as a 3x3 array filled with empty strings
steps.hint: Create a property called 'board' and set it equal to an array containing 3 sub-arrays, each with 3 empty string elements
steps.expectedOutcome: The BoardComponent class now has a board property initialized as a 3x3 grid of empty strings
successCriteria: The board property is defined and initialized as a 3x3 array with empty strings
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your board property is initialized as a 3x3 array with all positions containing empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The board property should be initialized as an array containing 3 sub-arrays, each with 3 empty string elements.

steps.title: Initialize current player state
steps.instruction: Add a currentPlayer property to the BoardComponent class and initialize it to 'X'.
steps.hint: Add the property declaration inside the class, similar to how you added the board property. Initialize it with the string value 'X'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BoardComponent class will have a currentPlayer property initialized to 'X' to track whose turn it is.
successCriteria: The BoardComponent class contains a currentPlayer property set to 'X'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the currentPlayer property is initialized to the string 'X'.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a currentPlayer property inside the class and set its initial value to 'X'.

steps.title: Initialize game over state
steps.instruction: Add a gameOver property to the BoardComponent class and initialize it to false
steps.hint: Add the gameOver property after the currentPlayer property, using the same syntax pattern
steps.expectedOutcome: The BoardComponent class will have a gameOver property initialized to false to track whether the game has ended
successCriteria: The gameOver property is declared in the BoardComponent class and initialized to false
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the gameOver property is initialized to false to indicate the game is initially active.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gameOver property should be added as a class property initialized to false. This will track whether the game has ended.

steps.title: Implement ngOnInit method
steps.instruction: Add an ngOnInit method to the BoardComponent class that calls a resetBoard method
steps.hint: The ngOnInit method is a lifecycle hook that runs after component initialization. It should call this.resetBoard() to set up the initial game state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BoardComponent class now has an ngOnInit method that calls resetBoard to initialize the game state
successCriteria: ngOnInit method is added to BoardComponent class and calls this.resetBoard()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your ngOnInit method calls this.resetBoard() to set up the initial game state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method should be added to the BoardComponent class and call this.resetBoard() method.

steps.title: Create resetBoard method
steps.instruction: Add a resetBoard method to the BoardComponent class that resets the board to an empty 3x3 grid, sets currentPlayer back to 'X', and sets gameOver to false.
steps.hint: Create a method that reinitializes all three state properties to their starting values - board as a 3x3 array of empty strings, currentPlayer as 'X', and gameOver as false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BoardComponent class now has a resetBoard method that can restore the game to its initial state by resetting all three properties.
successCriteria: A resetBoard method is defined that sets board to a 3x3 array of empty strings, currentPlayer to 'X', and gameOver to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your resetBoard method resets all three properties: board, currentPlayer, and gameOver.
steps.feedbackWrong: The resetBoard method should reset board to a 3x3 empty array, currentPlayer to 'X', and gameOver to false. Check that you're resetting all state properties.

steps.title: Create makeMove method
steps.instruction: Create a makeMove method that takes row and column parameters and updates the board state when a valid move is made.
steps.hint: The method should check if the position is empty, update the board array at the given position with the current player, and switch to the next player.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BoardComponent class will have a makeMove method that accepts row and column parameters and handles game logic.
successCriteria: A makeMove method is defined that takes row and column parameters and contains logic to update the board state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start on the makeMove method. Make sure it takes both row and column parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The makeMove method should be a method inside the BoardComponent class that accepts row and column parameters.

steps.title: Add move validation logic
steps.instruction: Add validation logic inside the makeMove method to check if the selected cell is empty and the game is not over before allowing the move
steps.hint: Use conditional statements to check if board[index] is empty (null, undefined, or empty string) and if gameOver is false before proceeding with the move logic
steps.expectedOutcome: The makeMove method contains validation to ensure moves are only allowed on empty cells when the game is active
successCriteria: Validation logic checks that the cell is empty and the game is not over before allowing moves
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start on validation. Make sure to check both that the cell is empty and the game is not over.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation should check if the selected cell is empty and if the game is still active before allowing the move.

steps.title: Add player switching logic
steps.instruction: Inside the makeMove method, after the move validation logic, add code to switch the currentPlayer from 'X' to 'O' or from 'O' to 'X'
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator or if-else statement to toggle currentPlayer between the two values after a valid move is made
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: toggling between two values
this.isDay = this.isDay ? false : true;
steps.expectedOutcome: The makeMove method will alternate the currentPlayer between 'X' and 'O' after each valid move
successCriteria: Player switching logic is added to toggle currentPlayer between 'X' and 'O'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with the player switching. Make sure to toggle between exactly 'X' and 'O' values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The player switching logic needs to alternate currentPlayer between 'X' and 'O'. Try using a ternary operator or if-else statement.

steps.title: Create board display template
steps.instruction: Add a template property to the BoardComponent class that contains nested divs using *ngFor to display the 3x3 board grid
steps.hint: Create a template property that returns HTML with a div for the board container and nested divs that loop through the board array to display each cell
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: template with nested loops template: `
{{item}}
`
steps.expectedOutcome: The BoardComponent class will have a template property that displays the board state as a 3x3 grid using Angular's *ngFor directive
successCriteria: A template property is added with HTML that uses *ngFor to loop through the board array and display each cell in a grid layout
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your template uses *ngFor to loop through the board array and displays each cell.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain HTML with *ngFor directive to display the board array as a grid. Check that you're looping through the board property.

steps.title: Wire click events to makeMove
steps.instruction: Add (click) event handlers to each button in the board template that call makeMove with the cell index
steps.hint: Use Angular's (click) event binding syntax on each button element. Pass the index i to makeMove when a cell is clicked.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: binding click events with parameters
<button (click)="handleClick(0)">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each button in the board template will have a click handler that calls makeMove with the cell index
successCriteria: Each button has a (click) event handler that calls makeMove with the index parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure each button has the (click) event handler that passes the index to makeMove.
steps.feedbackWrong: add (click) event binding to each button element. The handler should call makeMove with the index parameter.
